text:
Ashley Nguyen: Heads-up — several on-prem customers are hitting hairpin issues when we surface private endpoints into their VPCs. I'm sketching two options: 1)Documented DNAT/SNAT guidance for customer edge (hairpinless via DNAT) so we preserve src IP and avoid conntrack storms; 2)Offer an optional managed lightweight relay/proxy inside the customer's subnet (Redwood-managed, small footprint) to avoid requiring customer NAT changes. Want tradeoffs and a short rollout plan.

Raj Patel: Can you paste a recent error pattern? Is this conntrack exhaustion or TCP RSTs?

Ashley Nguyen: Mostly SYN retransmits followed by RSTs at scale. We also see conntrack high-water alerts on smaller NAT gateways during bursts (esp when customers have lots of short-lived requests).

Marta Lopez: DNAT is least infra on our side but requires customers to add rules (and some orgs won't allow). Relay buys us operational control but expands our trust surface and adds per-tenant state/metrics.

Chris Kim: Relay cost: the proxy itself is lightweight (TCP forwarding + optional TLS passthrough). Main questions: do we terminate TLS or passthrough? Termination lets us implement optimizations but is a compliance headache for some customers.

Devin O'Connor: Could we do a hybrid auto-mode: attempt hairpinless routing first, and fallback to relay only for tenants that actually hit conntrack/rst thresholds? That would limit relay footprint.

Ashley Nguyen: Thinking configwise, something like:
```
egress_mode: auto
hairpin_policy:
  prefer_dnat: true
  relay_fallback: true
  preserve_src_ip: true
```
This gives us deterministic behavior and a clear signal to support teams.

SRE-Bot: Note: enabling per-tenant relay increases metric cardinality and alert noise; recommend hard limits and aggregated metrics.

Raj Patel: Security question: DNAT preserves src IP, but does it break any mTLS/cert-related assumptions? If TLS peer identity is tied to source network ranges in any tenant rulebooks, we need to surface that to customers.

Marta Lopez: Ops plan idea: enable for 3 pilot customers, collect conntrack/latency/5xx deltas, then expand to 10. Add a circuit-breaker: if errors increase >5% within 30m, flip to relay or disable.

Chris Kim: +1 on pilot. Also add IPv6/NAT64 tests — some tenants use IPv6-only stacks and hit different pathologies.

Devin O'Connor: I'll spin a dev spike: daemonset 'egress-relay-proto' with ENV ENABLE_DNAT=true and a test fixture that pumps 20k short connections. Will post perf numbers.

Ashley Nguyen: Action items: Devin spike (this week), Marta draft runbook & pilot comms, Raj audit cert/mTLS edge-cases, Chris add IPv6/NAT64 e2e. I'll schedule a 30m RFC follow-up next Tue to lock default behavior. @here

Raj Patel: ack

Marta Lopez: ack

SRE-Bot: deploy-bot: canary cluster created for 'egress-relay-proto' — view: https://canary.internal/redwood/egress-relay-proto (internal)

Chris Kim: Also, let's capture a minimal rollback plan in the runbook: 1) disable relay for tenant, 2) revert route advertisement, 3) revoke temporary DNAT guidance. Short runbook will save ops during pilot.

Ashley Nguyen: Absolutely. I'll include a rollback checklist in the RFC follow-up. Thanks all.
